title: Split model ingestion into ingest-protocol, format-translator, and lazy-activation stages
creator: Alex Moran
description: Background: Our current model ingestion path attempts to do format detection, weight translation, tokenizer initialization, and eager weight activation in a single synchronous path. This causes high tail latency for first inference, makes format adapters tightly coupled to tokenizer boot logic, and increases cognitive load for onboarding new checkpoint formats. Goal: Break the monolith into three clear stages: 1) ingest-protocol layer that negotiates transport and manifest versions, 2) pluggable format-translator that normalizes weight shards and manifests into a canonical internal artifact (Manifest v2), and 3) lazy-activation/activation-proxy that defers heavy weight decoding and memory pinning until the model is first used (and supports staged activation). This ticket drives the refactor, tests, and documentation updates for the new contract while preserving backward compatibility via a compatibility shim.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest-protocol accepts existing checkpoint bundles and emits a normalized Manifest v2 with deterministic metadata fields (shard map, checksums, tokenizer pointer).
Format-translator interface is pluggable and has adapters for 'legacy-ckpt', 'sharded-tf', and 's3-snapshot' with unit tests covering byte-for-byte mapping where applicable.

Tokenizer initialization is decoupled from format-translator: tokenizer bootstrap becomes an asynchronous step invoked from the activation-proxy, with a clear API to request vocab/merges without forcing weight decoding.
Lazy-activation reduces first-request median CPU work for large models (>= 13B) by at least 30% compared to baseline measured on staging cluster.
No customer-facing API changes; existing model pinning and rollout policies continue to work without change.
Compatibility shim exists and is exercised by integration tests that load a variety of historical checkpoints used in production.
implementation_steps: Design ingest-protocol proto/JSON shape and agree on normalized Manifest v2 fields (owner: Priya).
Add a format-translator registry with a stable adapter interface and implement adapters for three high-priority formats (owner: backend-model-team).
Implement activation-proxy that defers tensor deserialization and exposes 'activate_shard' with progress hooks for console tracing (owner: runtime-team).
Update tokenizer bootstrap to provide a lightweight vocab/merge query API; remove tokenizer side-effects from format adapters.
Create integration tests (small/medium/large) that exercise cold-start, warm-start, and concurrent activations.
Run load tests on staging to collect latency tail and memory usage; iterate on prefetch heuristics.
Document the new adapter contract and provide a migration guide for model-onboarding in Confluence and the devbook.
Deprecate old monolithic ingestion code paths and add a feature flag to toggle the new pipeline for rollout.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting — aligned on three-stage split and agreed manifest fields. Action: Priya to write manifest draft.
2026-03-02: Prototype registry and adapter interface pushed to experimental branch. https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3412
2026-03-05: Initial activation-proxy spike validated lazy deserialization approach on a 7B model; observed ~35% CPU reduction on first request in the spike.
2026-03-09: Tokenizer bootstrap API spec completed; removed tokenizer side-effects from 'legacy-ckpt' adapter in prototype.
2026-03-11: Integration tests added for 'legacy-ckpt' and 'sharded-tf' adapters. Test failing intermittently due to race in shard manifest resolution — investigating.
2026-03-12: Opted for manifest-level lock (short-term) to mitigate race; long-term plan to use lease coordinator. Added ENG-190241 to track lease coordinator work.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incompatible manifest fields could break older ingestion clients. Mitigation: compatibility shim that translates old manifests to Manifest v2 and exhaustive integration tests.
Risk: Lazy activation could increase tail latency for very bursty workloads. Mitigation: prefetch heuristic and activation timeout with fallback to eager activation policy per model config.

Risk: Tokenizer decoupling might surface subtle differences in tokenization results when format adapters previously applied preprocessing. Mitigation: provide automated tokenization regression tests and a tokenizer-compatibility flag for opt-in strict mode.
Risk: Larger memory fragmentation during staged activation. Mitigation: activation proxy will perform capacity-aware scheduling and optionally coalesce activation tasks.
